title: unify-sdks-auth-retries-streaming-ergonomics-parity-vbump
author: Ava Chen
release_notes: Unifies auth and retry behavior across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs; improves streaming ergonomics; parity fixes and version bumps for all SDKs.
description: Motivation: We have ongoing drift between SDK languages in how auth tokens, retry semantics, and streaming APIs behave. This causes customer confusion and intermittent production issues when different language clients hit the same Redwood endpoints. This PR unifies auth and retry behavior, improves streaming ergonomics (single-call streaming helpers + backpressure-friendly iterators), fixes parity gaps discovered in internal audits, and bumps SDK package versions. Changes here implement the cross-language spec in ENG-4281 and follow the ergonomics proposals in ENG-4293. Work done: 1) Standardized auth: token refresh hooks and consistent credential fallback order across Python/TS/Go; introduced a thin credentials interface implemented in each SDK. 2) Retries: unified idempotency rules and a shared retry backoff config surface; TLS/transport error handling aligned with server-side transient markers. 3) Streaming: added high-level streaming iterators and helper utilities (Python: StreamingClient.stream_messages(), TS: streamMessages(), Go: StreamMessages(ctx, opts)). Helpers expose a common cancel/close ergonomics and optional auto-retry for resumed streams. 4) Parity fixes: matched Python and TS request/response shapes for function-calling and tool-calls; fixed a bug where Go SDK would drop trailing partial events for chunked responses. 5) Version bumps: Python -> 0.18.0, TypeScript -> 0.22.1, Go -> v0.9.0. Checklist: - [x] Implement shared spec and interfaces - [x] Add unit and integration tests per language - [x] Update docs and migration notes - [x] Run perf canary for streaming paths - [x] Bump package metadata and publish drafts Testing summary: unit tests and language-specific integration suites were added/updated; streaming e2e exercised under Canary with stable latency and no regression in p95. Related: references PR #70678, PR #78901 for earlier auth parity work. See linked Linear ENG-4281 and ENG-4293 for discussion and design notes.
